defining-boundaries-types.alt: Six small sketches, each with a red boundary line. Antecedent: the line is drawn before many settlers live there. Subsequent: a winding line drawn after settlement. Consequent: a line between two groups of houses of different colors, following a cultural line. Superimposed: a line drawn by outsiders through the middle of one group. Geometric: a straight line along 49 degrees north. Relict: a dashed gray line, a former boundary that no longer works. A note says one boundary can fit more than one type.
